data.title: Every rule reads one mdast tree parsed once per file
data.description: Rules query a shared syntax tree instead of scanning raw lines with their own regexes

data.title: Generated markdown is gated like hand-written markdown
data.description: Rendered output passes the same gates, and a finding there is fixed in its source or template

data.title: Fixes splice source slices and never re-stringify the tree
data.description: An edit replaces a byte range with text built from source slices, so untouched bytes stay identical

data.title: A fixer refuses whenever the input is ambiguous
data.description: An unfixable case leaves the source untouched and the finding reported, never a best guess

data.title: Every fix is verified against a content fingerprint and an expected shape
data.description: A lost word throws, and an unexpected tree shape refuses the edit before it is applied

data.title: Sentence length is reported and never autofixed
data.description: PG002 has no fixer, because shortening a sentence is a decision about what it means

data.title: An em-dash pair becomes parentheses and a lone em-dash becomes a colon
data.description: PG004 rewrites only the two dash patterns whose replacement punctuation is unambiguous

data.title: Each rule lives in its own file with its check and its fix together
data.description: A rule module exports its id, summary, check and optional fix, and a registry lists them in order

data.title: Adversarial and property tests gate every change to fix behaviour
data.description: Fix behaviour is proven by exact fixtures, hostile inputs and generated documents, all without mocks

data.title: A sentence length finding estimates clauses to guide a split
data.description: PG002 reports potential clauses and a target sentence count, steering a rewrite away from compression

data.title: Each rule carries a category, and RULES.md is held true by a test
data.description: Rules are tagged sentence, list or punctuation, and their documented examples run through the real fixer

data.title: Node runs a bundle built at publish time, and Bun runs the source
data.description: The npm package ships Node bundles of the CLI and library that are built when it is packed, and git never tracks them

data.title: Releases publish to npm from GitHub Actions through trusted publishing
data.description: The Publish workflow releases @jpeakai/prose-gates to npm with provenance and no stored token

data.title: Main changes only through pull requests, and releases run only from main
data.description: Main is protected so every change lands by a pull request that passes CI, and only main can publish

data.title: A check and a fix both read one context built once per document
data.description: Both halves of a rule read one RuleContext, so a check and its fix can never disagree about the document

data.title: A module groups functions by what they take, not by who calls them
data.description: Shared code sits in the layer whose data it reads, and the layers import strictly downwards

data.title: A rule id is its category followed by a short name
data.description: Rules are named category-short-name, such as sentence-one-per-line, instead of by a number

data.title: An optional config file switches rules off and sets their options
data.description: A config is checked against the loaded rules, and a rule that is off loses both its halves

data.title: A plugin rule is a built-in rule with a namespace, and the plugin names it
data.description: A plugin is { meta, rules }, its rules see the built-in context, and its ids carry a namespace

data.title: A plugin fixer is held to the same proof as a built-in one
data.description: Plugin fixers are allowed, every edit is verified, and a malformed edit is refused before it is spliced

data.title: A plugin adds a category by declaring it
data.description: A new one-word category is declared in meta.categories, and a word is declared once

data.title: Plugins and local rules load on their own from declared sources
data.description: Local rule files and declared plugin dependencies load with no config, and every run says so

data.title: Frontmatter is a read-only view that built-in rules never see
data.description: DocModel.frontmatter lists the top-level string keys of a YAML block, and built-in rules stay exempt

data.title: Every deliberate failure is a named error class with a stable code
data.description: Usage errors exit 2 and plugin errors exit 1, each class carrying a code and the fields to act on

data.title: Strict loading is the default, lenient and validated loading are opt-in and loud
data.description: A lenient run skips a failed plugin and names it, and a validation run reports every failure and runs no engine

data.title: A local rule may be TypeScript where the runtime can import it
data.description: .ts and .mts rules are imported as they are, and a runtime that cannot says how to fix it

data.title: Rules may be async, checks run concurrently, and fixers run in priority order
data.description: The engines are async, checks overlap, fixers are awaited one at a time, and the order stays a hand-kept list

data.title: A frontmatter edit is verified by comparing the YAML data before and after
data.description: A fixer may rewrite frontmatter if the YAML data is unchanged, and the view walks the whole document

data.title: The docs site is assembled from the real documents and deploys only from main
data.description: MkDocs Material builds from a copy of the repo's own layout, so the prose gates keep reading the real files

data.title: A paragraph over its sentence budget is reported with topic guidance and never autofixed
data.description: A paragraph over 5 sentences fails, and it runs after the list rules, and names its topics and breaks

data.title: Code complexity is gated by Biome rules that fail the build
data.description: Cognitive complexity, parameter count, test nesting and function length in src fail make check past fixed limits

data.title: The docs site wears the OsakaNights theme, copied in from jpai-mermaidjs-lint
data.description: The theme folder is vendored into site-theme/, pulled in with INHERIT, and its tokens are checked on every build

data.title: A paragraph carries a language view of its sentences and words, built on first read
data.description: ParagraphView.language holds sentences, words, tags and lemmas for every rule, plugins included

data.title: The clause count is the larger of the marker count and the verb phrases compromise finds
data.description: sentence-word-budget-exceeded counts clauses from punctuation and marker words, or from verbs, whichever finds more

data.title: Finding messages are measured by agent evals that never gate the build
data.description: Agents fix seed documents under pytest-xharness-eval, graded by the gates, to score each message

data.title: A project's GLOSSARY.md or CONCEPTS.md is read as its concept model, and the language view names its terms
data.description: Each H2 is a concept, each Mermaid edge a relation, and every sentence lists the concepts it mentions

data.title: sentence-one-per-line reports several sentences on one line, as its fixer splits them
data.description: A rule's check reports every paragraph its fixer would change, so a passing file is never rewritten by --fix

data.title: The Example Pages are rendered from the golden fixtures and a committed Sweep Snapshot
data.description: The site's examples of fixes and agent rewrites are generated, never written by hand, so they cannot drift from the code

data.title: A text view carries the same lazy language view as a paragraph
data.description: TextView.language reads a text node's value as English on first use, so prose outside a paragraph can be read too

data.title: A run with --no-concepts leaves the concept file unread
data.description: The flag gives every document an empty concept model, so a glossary in another shape cannot stop the run

data.title: A comma-joined run of three or more inline code spans is a hidden list, and plain words stay prose
data.description: The check flags the run anywhere, and the fix promotes it only when it closes a sentence
